title: Power Automate: generate documents from SharePoint document generation forms
summary: Hold: the briefing treats connector licensing and data-policy coverage as unpublished even though Microsoft's platform rules cover the SharePoint connector and its operations. It also omits a navigation group from the admin path and makes unsupported assurances about administrator action and overly broad claims about access to generated files.

claims.claim: Generate document from form (Preview) creates documents by mapping input data to fields in a document generation template.
claims.quote: Generate document from form (Preview) creates documents by mapping input data to a document generation template and saves the output to a SharePoint library.

claims.claim: The action saves generated documents to a SharePoint library.
claims.quote: Generate document from form (Preview) creates documents by mapping input data to a document generation template and saves the output to a SharePoint library.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the action returns the generated document with metadata such as location and status.
claims.quote: The action works by mapping input data to template fields and returns the generated document along with file metadata such as location and status.

claims.claim: The roadmap gives contracts, invoices, letters and reports as example uses.
claims.quote: This capability supports scenarios such as creating contracts, invoices, letters, or reports using structured templates and form-driven inputs.

claims.claim: Microsoft requires no administrator action.
claims.quote: Searched: "document generation forms" "no admin action"; "document generation forms" "default" "rollout". Opened structured-document-generation and SharePoint connector guidance/reference; none states that no admin action is required.
claims.fix: Remove 'no admin action is required by Microsoft' from the summary. Retain the body's narrower statement that Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that data policies governing the SharePoint connector apply to this action.
claims.quote: Any Power Apps or Power Automate resource that includes an existing connection with a connector in the Non-business data group, isn't allowed to establish connections with SharePoint or Salesforce connectors.

Remove the corresponding data-policy applicability question. This does not claim that SharePoint itself is blockable.
